short: the JVM's -Xlog system (java 9): pick tags and levels, an output and decorators. GC logs are -Xlog:gc*.
a snapshot of every object in the heap and every reference between them, in an .hprof file. how you find leaks.
what would become garbage if one object disappeared: itself plus everything reachable only through it.
a tree of objects where each parent is on every path from the GC roots to its children. sorted by retained size, it points at leaks.
a JVM feature that breaks the process's non-heap memory down by category. -XX:NativeMemoryTracking=summary, then jcmd VM.native_memory.
a ByteBuffer whose bytes live outside the heap, freed only when the GC collects its small heap object. capped by -XX:MaxDirectMemorySize.
resident set size: memory pages actually in RAM. what top and container limits count, and always more than -Xmx.
